title: Filling in a Form
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the vocabulary was reconstructed from context and standard German. The sample form exercise at the end of the video could not be recovered from the captions, so it is replaced by new practice items.
objectives: I can understand the common fields of a German form
I can fill in personal data: name, address, date of birth, nationality, job
I can write dates and addresses in the German way
I can fill in a form for a trip or a course

expressions.de: Bitte füllen Sie das Formular aus.

grammar.title: Fields on a form have no article
grammar.body: In the vocabulary list we learn nouns with their articles (**der Nachname**, **die Adresse**). On the form itself they are written **without** article: *Nachname, Vorname, Adresse, Beruf*. **ausfüllen** is a separable verb: *Ich fülle das Formular aus.*

grammar.title: Writing an address
grammar.body: In Germany the order is: **street, house number, postcode, city**. Write the street first and the number after it. The postcode (PLZ) has five digits and comes before the city name. Sometimes the country (**das Land**) is asked separately.

grammar.title: Writing the date
grammar.body: In German you write the **day first, then the month, then the year**: **Tag – Monat – Jahr**. For *Geburtsdatum* write for example **14.03.1995**. The place of birth is **der Geburtsort** (for example: Berlin).
grammar.ar: ترتيب التاريخ: اليوم ثم الشهر ثم السنة.

grammar.title: Personal details: nationality, language, family
grammar.body: **Staatsangehörigkeit:** deutsch, französisch ... **Muttersprache:** Arabisch, Englisch, ... **Familienstand:** ledig, verheiratet, geschieden. You can also be asked about **Kinder** (children). For **Geschlecht** choose *weiblich* or *männlich*.

examples.de: Ich bin verheiratet und habe zwei Kinder.
examples.en: I am married and have two children.

grammar.title: Forms for trips and courses
grammar.body: A form at the travel agent or hotel asks for **Reiseziel**, **Abflug** (also *Abreise* or *Abfahrt*) and **Ankunft** (also *Anreise*). A form for a course or exam asks for **Prüfung**, **Kurs** and **Kursbeginn**. A club form may ask for your **Hobby**. At the end of every form you give **Ort, Datum** and **Unterschrift**.

mistakes.why: In German the order is day, month, year.
Street and house number first, then PLZ and city.

pronunciation.tip: Stress the first syllable of separable-verb nouns: *AN-kunft, AB-flug*.

lines.de: Guten Tag, ich möchte einen Kurs buchen.
lines.en: Good day, I would like to book a course.

lines.de: Gern. Bitte füllen Sie das Formular aus.
lines.en: Gladly. Please fill in the form.

lines.de: Mein Nachname ist Schmidt, mein Vorname ist David.
lines.en: My surname is Schmidt, my first name is David.

tip: Fill in forms in capital letters if the form asks for it, and always check name, date of birth and signature before you hand it in.

comprehension.q: In which order do you write an address in Germany?
In which order do you write the date?
What are three possible answers for Familienstand?
What do you give at the end of a form?

exercises.title: Match the form fields
exercises.instructions: Match the German field with its English meaning.

exercises.title: Which field is it?
exercises.instructions: Write the correct form field (with article) for each entry.

items.q: Bei der Adresse schreibt man zuerst die ___ und dann die Hausnummer.
Das Datum schreibt man: Tag, ___, Jahr.
Am Ende des Formulars schreibt man die ___. (signature)
Wer nicht verheiratet und nicht geschieden ist, ist ___.

exercises.title: Put the address in the right order
exercises.instructions: Write the address in the correct German order.

summary: A Formular has fields such as Nachname, Vorname, Adresse, Geburtsdatum, Beruf.
Address order: Straße, Hausnummer, PLZ, Ort. Date order: Tag, Monat, Jahr.
Family status: ledig, verheiratet, geschieden. Gender: weiblich / männlich.
Travel and course forms ask for Reiseziel, Abflug, Ankunft, Kursbeginn.
Finish every form with Ort, Datum and Unterschrift.
